rawFindings.title: Regression in proxy port resolution logic
rawFindings.explanation: The change replaced a conditional port resolution block with a simplified expression that can incorrectly assign the port. Specifically, the new code uses proxyDetails.port || config.port || (protocol check), which means if proxyDetails.port is undefined but config.port is defined, config.port is used regardless of protocol. The previous code correctly prioritized protocol-based default ports over config.port when proxyDetails.port is missing, maintaining protocol logic. This can cause proxy con
rawFindings.suggestion: Revert to the prior port resolution logic to preserve protocol-based default ports, i.e., use nested if-else to set port based on proxyDetails.port, or protocol default (https:443, http:80), then fallback to config.port.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Proxy target https://somehost without explicit port and config.port=9877 resolves port to 9877 instead of 443, causing failure to connect to correct proxy endpoint.
